title: Command Handoff and Ops Manifest
meeting_header: Date: 2026-06-25 | Time: 10:00 PDT | Duration: 62 min | Location: Zoom | Recording: yes | Deck: https://redwood.internal/decks/ops-manifest-2026-06.pdf
summary: Town-hall style leadership huddle focused on operational responsibilities for H2, a lightweight handoff of command rotations, and initiatives to reduce inference latency surprises. High-level Q&A, hiring & culture update, and three concrete ops playbooks to be distributed.
topics: Audit / compliance touchpoints for Private deployments
action_items: Miguel: Publish incident runbook v1 to docs and link in #ops by 2026-07-02
Daniel: Kick off two-week kernel optimization spike and share initial metrics 2026-07-09
Priya: Assemble a cross-functional benchmarking prompt set and invite QE by 2026-07-06
Lila: Post updated on-call rotation calendar and escalation matrix by 2026-06-29
Nora: Share compliance checklist for a SOC2 readiness check with product teams by 2026-07-12
next_steps: Leads to review playbooks and acknowledge in the all-hands channel
Schedule a follow-up firebreak next Friday for spike readouts
Send trimmed deck and incident templates to the company
transcript: [00:00] Ava: Okay everyone good morning, uh startin a little early but thanks for joining—we'll kick off in a minute
[00:15] Ava: Welcome to the "Command Handoff and Ops Manifest" town-hall. Quick run of the deck, then Q&A. We're recording this call.

[00:28] Daniel: Hi all, quick context. We've seen two incidents last month where KV cache eviction caused tail latency spikes during steady load. We're making some changes to runtime routing and also changing our canary thresholds.
[00:45] Miguel: Right, and that ties to the command handoff—ops responsibilities need clearer owner for the kernel/quant path. I'm proposing a two-week on-call rotation for infra leads.
[01:02] Tom (SRE): Miguel, when you say rotation, do you mean 24/7 primary? We already have nights covered but seams around weekends are fuzzy, sorry — seams, I mean seams, uh seams in coverage.
[01:18] Lila: We'll roll the rotation into the existing on-call calendar, yes. Also HR will support with overtime and on-call compensation clarifications.
[01:36] Priya: From product: we want a predictable latency envelope. Target is p95 < 120ms for generator small models, p95 < 200ms for larger chat flows under normal load. We need measurable probes.
[01:54] Soumya: I'll own the synthetic probes. We'll generate realistic chat traces and measure across regions. Might be noisy initially, but that's okay.
[02:10] Ava: Great. A couple of behavioral asks: keep incident comms to the channel #ops-incident with the postmortem template. Use the new severity rubric in the playbook.
[02:28] Rachel: Quick Q — how strict is the fallback policy? Are we going to auto-fallback to quantized variants on overloads or keep manual gate?

[02:44] Daniel: We prefer automated fallback with human-in-loop for canary rollouts. If model quality drops beyond threshold, trigger rollback. We'll surface quality regression alerts from Redwood Optimize — literally an alert to teams.
[03:02] Miguel: Action here: we need canary + automatic fallback + metric thresholds in the same playbook. I'll draft that and attach.

[03:18] Ethan: On cost — we ran a quick analysis. Burstable Dedicated nodes give better cost/lower p95 for consistent workloads, but hosted bursts are cheaper for spiky traffic. Need product to decide burning vs reserved capacity.
[03:36] Priya: We'll present two workload archetypes to the FinOps folks — steady-state customer inference vs. spiky interactive products.
[03:52] Ava: Hiring and org changes: we're creating a Shared Reliability Pod of five engineers to focus on inference runtime optimizations. Miguel will hire two senior infra engineers this quarter.
[04:07] Lila: Mic drop on priorities: make sure your hiring scorecards map to the pod competencies. We'll fast-track interviews for referrals.

[04:22] Nora (Legal): Quick compliance note — Private deployments now require a slightly different audit trace retention. We're updating the checklist. We'll need product sign-off for customer contracts.
[04:38] Priya: We'll sync with Nora; need to confirm data residency options for EMEA customers too.
[04:52] Ava: Alright slides 6–8: the three playbooks. Incident response, capacity planning, and benchmarking. Miguel — walk us through incident response briefly.

[05:08] Miguel: Incident playbook v0.1: triage, assign, communicate, mobilize, mitigate, postmortem. We added a shortcut for common KV cache problems: clear prefix and warm caches when safe. There's a checklist to escalate to kernel owners at severity 2.
[05:30] Tom: One note: the 'clear prefix' step can remove useful warm caches; needs a safeguard to prevent broad evictions. We should be able to target per-customer prefixes.
[05:46] Miguel: Agreed, I'll add targeted eviction steps and an audit log entry requirement.
[06:05] Daniel: On the optimization spike — we'll evaluate two kernel patches and one batching change. Expect bench results by next Friday. If they materially reduce p95 we'll roll to canary.
[06:22] Soumya: For benchmarking, we need a canonical prompt set that reflects both long-form generation and short completions. I'll coordinate with Priya's product scenarios.
[06:40] Rachel: How are we surfacing these benchmarks to customers? We sometimes get early inbound questions about performance guarantees.
[06:53] Ava: We'll include a concise benchmark page in the Console — model cards + observed p50/p95 under standard probes. Marketing will help craft the language so we don't overpromise.
[07:10] Priya: Also we should include a 'how to reproduce' folder for customers doing private deployments — sample configs and probe scripts.
[07:25] Ethan: Ops note — align autoscaling rules with the canary system so that we don't confuse autoscaler scale events with eruptive traffic spikes during rollouts.
[07:40] Miguel: Good call. I'll add a rollout-protected autoscaling window in the playbook.
[08:00] Ava: Culture check — Lila, anything to surface from people ops?
[08:06] Lila: We're seeing burnout in some SREs. Need better rotation handoff docs and protected off-ramps. We'll also pilot a 'no-meeting day' for on-call teams after high-severity incidents.
[08:22] Rachel: That would be helpful. Also request: can we have an incident retro template that doesn't require a huge write-up? Quick 10-min riff is more likely to happen.
[08:36] Lila: We'll provide both a short and long template in docs.
[08:50] Ava: Questions from the chat: 'Will Dedicated customers get priority routing in multi-tenant overloads?'
[08:57] Daniel: Yes, routing policy will prefer Dedicated capacity for reserved customers; hosted will be fallback. We need to document failover order and latency impacts.
[09:15] Soumya: Small note — our synthetic probes should include token distribution skew since some prompts are heavy system tokens which change perf characteristics.
[09:32] Miguel: We'll add sequence length buckets to the benchmark.
[09:50] Ava: Okay time for a lightning demo of the incident dashboard — slide 12. Miguel take it away.

[10:00] Miguel: Demo voice: the dashboard pulls p50/p95, active incidents, and shows canary rollouts with timelines. It's rough but useful. Note: some model names are obfuscated in the demo gif, apologies — the recording sometimes mangles names.
[10:23] Tom: I saw a typo in the dashboard query that double-counts warm cache hits. I'll send a suggested fix.
[10:38] Miguel: Thanks Tom, send it in the PR, I'll review.
[10:50] Ava: Back to strategy — H2 OKRs: reduce unit cost by 12%, improve p95 by 20% for interactive flows, and cut incident MTTR by 30%.
[11:08] Priya: We'll align product epics to those OKRs and provide a roadmap snapshot by end of week.
[11:22] Ethan: On the cost number — are we including network and storage egress in the 12%?
[11:30] Ava: Good catch — yes total cost of inference including storage & egress. FinOps will provide a baseline.
[11:45] Lila: Hiring update: transfer approvals came through for two senior infra roles plus a reliability program manager.
[11:56] Rachel: Will the program manager be embedded in infra or cross-functional?
[12:02] Lila: Cross-functional but dotted to infra for priority alignment.
[12:15] Nora: From legal: the compliance checklist will require an updated data processing agreement for some Private customers. We'll circulate the template.
[12:28] Ava: Alright let's move to rapid-fire Q&A. Type questions in chat and we'll call them out.
[12:35] [chat question] 'Any changes to SLAs in Dedicated contracts?'
[12:40] Daniel: No SLA changes planned; we may add an optional lower-latency tier with a different pricing model.
[12:52] [chat question] 'Can we get hints for model quantization impacts on hallucination rates?'
[12:58] Priya: That's a research question — we'll run targeted evals and tie any regressions to the quality monitoring system, then include guidance in the Optimize recommendations.
[13:15] Ava: Closing remarks — we need everyone to read the three playbooks this week and ack in the channel. If you own an action item, add your name to the doc.
[13:28] Miguel: I'll open the PR for the incident runbook after the call.
[13:36] Ava: Thanks all. Recap: publish docs, start optimization spike, update on-call, and hire two infra engineers. Meeting adjourned.
[13:46] [post-meeting chatter] Ethan: Quick note to Priya — can we add the sample user flows to the benchmarking set?
[13:52] Priya: Yes, ping me and I'll share the list.
[14:00] [end of recording]
